actual_focused_facts.text: [F1] Potential-pair formulas: for a pair $(\varphi,A)$ of class $C^m$, $m\ge1$, $E(\varphi,A)=-\nabla\varphi-\partial_tA$ and $B(\varphi,A)=\operatorname{curl}A$ are of class $C^{m-1}$, the transform of a $C^m$ pair by a $C^m$ generator is $T_\chi(\varphi,A)=(\varphi-\partial_t\chi,A+\nabla\chi)$ and is of class $C^{m-1}$ ([[def-em-potential-gauge-and-field-conventions]]); for a non-open $I$ the joint classes and the componentwise computations are read in the open-neighbourhood restriction convention of [[lem-em-joint-smooth-potentials]], whose relative time derivatives at included endpoints reproduce the two identities below pointwise on $\Omega\times I$.

[F2] Framework vocabulary: a potential representation of a field pair is a potential pair with that field pair, a gauge function of class $C^m$ has $m\ge2$, two pairs are gauge related when one is the gauge transform of the other, and the field pair of a representation is its physical content ([[def-em-gauge-transformation]]).

actual_focused_facts.text: [F3] Spherical-mean family of a smooth spacetime function: with $h$ as given and $d\Omega$ of total mass $4\pi$, the family $m(x,s,v):=\frac{1}{4\pi}\int_{S^2}h(x+sn,v)\,d\Omega(n)$ is of class $C^\infty$ on $\mathbb R^3\times\mathbb R\times[t_0,T]$ in the extension sense, and every word iterated partial derivative is obtained by differentiating the composed integrand under the sphere integral; the statement is local, assumes no decay, compact support or boundedness of $h$, and uses uniform bounds only on compact parameter sets ([[lem-em-spherical-mean-family-smoothness]]).

[F4] Spherical means of a fixed smooth datum: for $f\in C^\infty(\mathbb R^3)$ and $M_rf(x)=\frac{1}{4\pi}\int_{S^2}f(x+rn)\,d\Omega(n)$, $r\ge0$, the map $r\mapsto M_rf(x)$ is smooth for $r\ge0$ and satisfies the Euler-Poisson-Darboux identity $\partial_r^2M_rf+\frac{2}{r}\partial_rM_rf=\Delta M_rf$ for $r>0$, and $H_f(x,t):=t\,M_{ct}f(x)$, $t\ge0$, satisfies $\partial_t^2H_f=c^2\Delta H_f$, $H_f(\cdot,0)=0$ and $\partial_tH_f(\cdot,0)=f$; all identities are local and assume no decay of $f$ ([[lem-em-spherical-mean-wave-identity]]).

[F5] Parameter integrals: if $K\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ is compact, measurable and of finite Lebesgue measure, $a<b$, and $f,\partial_tf$ are continuous on a neighbourhood of $K\times[a,b]$, then $t\mapsto\int_Kf(x,t)\,dx$ is differentiable on $[a,b]$ with derivative $\int_K\partial_tf(x,t)\,dx$; the same holds, under the $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ convention of [[def-surface-integral-on-a-compact-c-one-hypersurface]], with surface measure on a fixed compact $C^1$ hypersurface in place of $K$; moving parameter sets and singularities crossing the integration set are excluded ([[lem-em-parameter-integrals]]).

actual_focused_facts.text: [F1] Retarded kernel: for every $h\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^3\times\mathbb R)$ the function $(K*h)(x,t)=\int_{\mathbb R^3}h(y,t-|x-y|/c)/(4\pi|x-y|)\,dy$ is well defined (absolutely convergent), of class $C^\infty$ on $\mathbb R^3\times\mathbb R$, and satisfies $W(K*h)=h$ pointwise. ([[lem-em-retarded-wave-kernel]] (b))

[F2] Gauge identities and the decoupling definition: for a potential pair of class $C^2$ jointly on an open set, $\operatorname{div}E=W\varphi-\partial_tG$ and $\operatorname{curl}B-c^{-2}\partial_tE=WA+\nabla G$ hold there, the source-free equations $\operatorname{div}B=0$ and $\operatorname{curl}E=-\partial_tB$ hold automatically for any potential pair, and if in addition $G=0$ then the sourced Maxwell system of [[post-em-vacuum-maxwell]] holds if and only if $W\varphi=\rho/\varepsilon_0$ and $WA=\mu_0J$; the fields $E,B$, the Lorenz divergence $G$ and the wave expression $W$ are those of [[def-em-potential-gauge-and-field-conventions]], and field regularity classes are those of [[def-em-fields]]. ([[pthm-em-lorenz-gauge-wave-form]] (a),(c))

[F3] Cauchy uniqueness: if $v\in C^2(\mathbb R^3\times[t_1,T'])$ is of class $C^2$ in the extension sense, satisfies $Wv=h$ on $\mathbb R^3\times(t_1,T')$ with $h\in C^\infty(\mathbb R^3\times[t_1,T'])$ in the extension sense, and has prescribed Cauchy data at $t_1$, then $v$ equals the solution constructed there. ([[thm-em-wave-cauchy-kirchhoff]] (b))

[F11] Parameter integrals: if $K$ is compact measurable of finite measure and $f,\partial_tf$ are continuous on a neighbourhood of $K\times[a,b]$, then $t\mapsto\int_Kf(x,t)\,dx$ is differentiable there with derivative $\int_K\partial_tf(x,t)\,dx$. ([[lem-em-parameter-integrals]])

[F13] The framework adopts the retarded branch of [[post-em-radiation-selection]]: the selected physical potential pair is the retarded one with no free addition, and the theorem below computes exactly that branch; it asserts no existence of its own. ([[post-em-radiation-selection]] (b),(c))

actual_focused_facts.text: [F5] Parameter integrals over a fixed compact measurable set of finite measure: if $K\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ is compact, measurable and of finite measure, if $a<b$, and if the real-valued $f$ and $\partial_tf$ are continuous on a neighbourhood of $K\times[a,b]$, then $t\mapsto\int_Kf(x,t)\,dx$ is differentiable at every $t\in(a,b)$ with derivative $\int_K\partial_tf(x,t)\,dx$ and has the corresponding one-sided relative derivatives at the endpoints of $[a,b]$; the lemma is stated pointwise in its one real parameter and explicitly asserts nothing for moving parameter sets or for singularities crossing $K$. Applying it once per parameter direction with its parameter renamed to $x_1,x_2,x_3$ or $t$ (all other variables held fixed), and iterating on the resulting integrals, yields the corresponding partial derivatives of a parameter integral whose integrand is smooth in all variables on a neighbourhood of the fixed $K$. ([[lem-em-parameter-integrals]])

[F8] Zero-data wave Cauchy problem of speed $c$ from time $t_0$ with source $h\in C^\infty(\mathbb R^3\times[t_0,T])$ in the extension sense: its solution is $u(x,t)=c^2\int_{t_0}^t(t-v)M_{c(t-v)}h(\cdot,v)(x)\,dv$ on $\mathbb R^3\times[t_0,T]$, it is $C^\infty$ there, and it satisfies $c^{-2}\partial_t^2u-\Delta u=h$; here $M_rh(x,v)=\frac1{4\pi}\int_{S^2}h(x+rn,v)\,d\Omega(n)$. actual_focused_facts.text: [F1] Far-zone expansion of [[thm-em-radiation-asymptotic-flux]] (b): with $\mathbf I(n,u)=\int_{B_a}J(y,u+n\cdot y/c)dy$, $\mathbf V=\partial_u\mathbf I$, $\mathbf E_{\mathrm{lead}}(n,u,r)=\frac{\mu_0}{4\pi r}n\times(n\times\mathbf V(n,u))$ and $\Gamma_E,\Gamma_B$ constants depending only on $a,c,\mu_0$ and the source suprema, for all $n\in S^2$, $u\in[t_0,T]$, $r\ge2a$ one has $|\mathbf E(rn,u+r/c)-\mathbf E_{\mathrm{lead}}(n,u,r)|\le\Gamma_E/r^2$ and $|\mathbf B(rn,u+r/c)-n\times\mathbf E_{\mathrm{lead}}(n,u,r)/c|\le\Gamma_B/r^2$. ([[thm-em-radiation-asymptotic-flux]] (b))

[F2] Retarded-time flux limit of [[thm-em-radiation-asymptotic-flux]] (c): for every $u\in[t_0,T]$, $\lim_{r\to\infty}\int_{S^2}r^2n\cdot S(rn,u+\tfrac rc)\,d\Omega(n)=\frac{\mu_0}{16\pi^2c}\int_{S^2}|n\times\mathbf V(n,u)|^2\,d\Omega(n)$, a limit at fixed retarded time; $d\Omega$ is the sphere surface measure, which equals the polar measure $\sigma$ on $S^2$. ([[thm-em-radiation-asymptotic-flux]] (c))

[F3] Energy flux reading: $S=E\times B/\mu_0$ is the Poynting energy-flux density of [[def-em-vacuum-energy-flux]], and the fixed-volume Poynting balance of [[pthm-em-poynting-balance]] contains $-\oint S\cdot n\,dS$, the negative of the outward field-energy flux, in the field-energy rate. ([[def-em-vacuum-energy-flux]], [[pthm-em-poynting-balance]])

[F5] Parameter integrals over a fixed compact set: if $f,\partial_tf$ are continuous on a neighbourhood of $K\times J$ with $K$ compact measurable of finite measure, then $t\mapsto\int_Kf$ is differentiable with derivative $\int_K\partial_tf$; iterating gives $C^\infty$ dependence for $C^\infty$ integrands. ([[lem-em-parameter-integrals]])
[F11] Shifted source moments: $V(n,u)=\int_{B_a}J_t(y,u+n\cdot y/c)dy=\partial_uI(n,u)$. ([[thm-em-radiation-asymptotic-flux]] (a),(b))

[F13] Compact smooth branch: for the same source class the retarded fields satisfy the smooth vacuum Maxwell equations and the total charge vanishes: $\int_{B_a}\rho(y,u)dy=0$ for every $u$, and the retarded pair is the adopted selected branch. ([[pthm-em-retarded-potentials]] (b),(f), [[post-em-radiation-selection]])

actual_focused_facts.text: [F1] Cauchy problem for the scalar wave equation ([[thm-em-wave-cauchy-kirchhoff]]): assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, let $c>0$, $t_0<T$, $a,b\in C^\infty(\mathbb R^3)$ and let $h$ be $C^\infty$ on $\mathbb R^3\times[t_0,T]$ in the extension sense, and let $u$ be the spherical-mean construction of that theorem. Then (a) $u$ is $C^\infty$ on $\mathbb R^3\times[t_0,T]$ in the extension sense, $Wu=h$ on $\mathbb R^3\times(t_0,T)$, $u(\cdot,t_0)=a$ and $\partial_tu(\cdot,t_0)=b$; (b) every $v\in C^2$ in the extension sense with the same $Wv=h$ and the same Cauchy data equals $u$; (c) if data agree on the closed ball $\overline B_{c(t_*-t_0)}(x_*)$ and the sources agree on the closed backward cone $K(x_*,t_*)$, the corresponding solutions agree at $(x_*,t_*)$ for every $x_*\in\mathbb R^3$ and $t_*\in[t_0,T]$; (d) if $a,b$ vanish off compact sets and $h(\cdot,v)$ vanishes off a fixed compact set contained in $\overline B_\rho(0)$, then $u(x,t)=0$ whenever $|x|>\rho+c(t-t_0)$.

[F4] Local Poynting identity ([[pthm-em-poynting-balance]](a)): for the jointly $C^1$ fields of the smooth branch with continuous sources on the laboratory region, the energy density $u$ and Poynting vector $S$ of [[def-em-vacuum-energy-flux]] satisfy $\partial_tu+\operatorname{div}S=-J\cdot E$; in particular on a source-free region $J=0$ one has $\partial_tu+\operatorname{div}S=0$.

[F6] Parameter integrals ([[lem-em-parameter-integrals]], set form): for $K\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ compact, Lebesgue measurable with $\lambda_n(K)<\infty$ and $f$, $\partial_tf$ continuous on an open neighbourhood of $K\times[a,b]$, the map $t\mapsto\int_Kf(x,t)\,dx$ is differentiable at every $t\in(a,b)$ with derivative $\int_K\partial_tf(x,t)\,dx$, and has the corresponding one-sided derivatives at the endpoints.

[F13] Spherical-mean wave identity ([[lem-em-spherical-mean-wave-identity]]): for $c>0$ and $f\in C^\infty(\mathbb R^3)$ the mean $M_rf(x)=\frac{1}{4\pi}\int_{S^2}f(x+rn)\,d\Omega(n)$ is smooth in $r\ge0$, satisfies the Euler-Poisson-Darboux identity, and $H_f(x,t)=t\,M_{ct}f(x)$ satisfies $\partial_t^2H_f=c^2\Delta H_f$, $H_f(\cdot,0)=0$, $\partial_tH_f(\cdot,0)=f$; the identities are local and need no decay of $f$.
